title: Triangulated compatibility of the evaluation-defined scalar Hom comparison
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, and use constant ring sheaves on the small etale site and the ordinary unbounded module derived categories $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)$. Write $F(T)=T\otimes_A^L B$, $H_A(K,M)=R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M)$, and similarly $H_B$. Define $v_{K,M}:FH_A(K,M)\to H_B(FK,FM)$ as the tensor–Hom transpose of $FH_A(K,M)\otimes_B^L FK\cong F(H_A(K,M)\otimes_A^L K)\xrightarrow{F\mathrm{ev}_A}FM$. For each fixed $M$, this is a natural transformation between contravariant exact functors of $K$, compatible with their canonical shift identifications: it gives a morphism of the reversed distinguished triangles for every distinguished triangle of $K$'s, including its connecting morphism and signs. Its isomorphism locus is a thick subcategory: it contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, shifts, cones, and direct summands. No flatness assumption on $B$ is imposed.

Notation and categorical conventions are those of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], [def-weil-triangulated-category].

proof.text: Work on the small étale site, in a universe containing its objects and module sheaves; write $A,B$ also for the constant ring sheaves. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $F=-\otimes_A^L B$ exists on the ordinary unbounded derived categories. Give it the counit-compatible shift $\sigma$ of [lem-sbc-derived-scalar-extension-counit-shift]; that result makes $(F,\sigma)$ exact and identifies $\sigma$ with the degreewise identity on termwise scalar extension of K-flat models. The identity geometric morphism with ring map $A\to B$ satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Its tensor comparison, inverted, gives $\mu_{U,V}:FU\otimes_B^L FV\xrightarrow{\sim}F(U\otimes_A^L V)$. On flat-term K-flat models its formula is $(x\otimes b)\otimes(y\otimes c)\mapsto(x\otimes y)\otimes bc$. Scalar coefficients have degree zero; this formula preserves both tensor degrees and every sign in the total differential. Hence it commutes with the tensor shift maps, including the simultaneous-shift cancellation used in Step 4. These statements concern derived scalar extension and require no flatness of $B$ over $A$.

proof.text:
For either coefficient sheaf $R=A,B$, the internal-Hom calculus [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] and [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(T,H_R(K,N))=H^0 H_R(T,H_R(K,N))=H^0 H_R(T\otimes_R^L K,N)=\operatorname{Hom}(T\otimes_R^L K,N).$$
Here $H^0$ means global hypercohomology. Their representative normalization is the chain currying of [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total]: if $P$ represents $K$, $I$ is K-injective representing $N$, and $h:T\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,I)$ with $T,P$ flat-term K-flat, uncurrying is $t\otimes p\mapsto h(t)(p)$. The Hom into $I$ computes the specified derived Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. This fixes evaluation $e_{R,K,N}$ as the transpose of its identity. With $H=H_A(K,M)$, define $v_K=v_{K,M}$ by
$$e_{B,FK,FM}(v_K\otimes1)=F(e_{A,K,M})\mu_{H,K}.$$
This is exactly the map in the item. The Hom calculus also says $H_R(-,N)$ is contravariantly exact, with its signed shift comparisons. Thus $\Phi(K)=FH_A(K,M)$ and $\Psi(K)=H_B(FK,FM)$ are additive contravariant exact functors, using the exact $F$ of Step 1.

Let $f:K'\to K$. The two maps $v_{K'}F(H_A(f,1))$ and $H_B(Ff,1)v_K$ from $FH_A(K,M)$ to $H_B(FK',FM)$ have the same transpose: after $\mu$, both are $F(e_{A,K,M}\circ(1\otimes f))$. This follows by inserting the defining evaluation identity from Step 2 and the naturality of $\mu$. The bijection of Step 2 therefore makes these maps equal. Thus $v:\Phi\to\Psi$ is natural on every derived morphism in $K$. The same argument for $g:M\to M'$ gives transpose $F(g\circ e_{A,K,M})$ on both sides and proves naturality in $M$ as well. This uses adjunction bijections in the full derived categories, not representatives of arbitrary derived arrows by chain maps.

proof.text:
Here is the evaluation shift sign, for $R=A$ or $B$. Choose a flat-term K-flat $P$ representing $K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and a K-injective $I$ representing $N$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Put $D=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,I)$, representing $H_R(K,N)$ by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Substitution in $d(f)=d_I f-(-1)^a f d_P$ [def-pur-hom-complex] shows that
$$s_R:H_R(K[1],N)\longrightarrow H_R(K,N)[-1]$$
is represented by $f\mapsto(-1)^a f$ in Hom degree $a$ (with source indices reindexed). The coefficients of the postcomposition and precomposition terms are respectively $(-1)^{a+1}$ and $-1$ on both sides of the chain-map equation. Define the natural cancellation $\tau_{U,V}:U[-1]\otimes^L V[1]\to U\otimes^L V$ by $u\otimes v\mapsto(-1)^a u\otimes v$ when $u$ has degree $a$ in $U[-1]$. The total tensor differential [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] verifies this chain isomorphism: both sides give coefficients $(-1)^a$ on $d_Uu\otimes v$ and $-1$ on $u\otimes d_Vv$. To check evaluation, resolve $D$ by a flat-term K-flat $T\xrightarrow{h}D$. The model $T[-1]\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P[1],I)$ is $s_R^{-1}h[-1]$. Its evaluation on $t\otimes p$ has sign $(-1)^a$, exactly the sign from $\tau$ followed by the original evaluation. Using the normalized currying of Step 2 gives
$$e_{R,K[1],N}=e_{R,K,N}\,\tau_{H_R(K,N),K}(s_R\otimes1).$$
This is an equality of maps in $D(R)$; the tensor models descend by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent].

proof.text:
Write $s_A=s_{A,K,M}$, and give $\Phi$ the shift comparison $\chi_\Phi:\Phi(K[1])\to\Phi(K)[-1]$ obtained by $F(s_A)$ then $\sigma$ for shift $-1$. Give $\Psi$ the comparison $\chi_\Psi:\Psi(K[1])\to\Psi(K)[-1]$ obtained by precomposition with $\sigma_K^{-1}:FK[1]\to F(K[1])$ and then $s_{B,FK,FM}$. We prove
$$\chi_\Psi v_{K[1]}=v_K[-1]\chi_\Phi.$$
Put $T=\Phi(K[1])$, $H=H_A(K,M)$. Compose either proposed map $T\to H_B(FK,FM)[-1]$ with $s_B^{-1}$ and transpose; injectivity of Step 2 reduces equality to maps $T\otimes_B^L FK[1]\to FM$. For the left side its transpose is
$$F(e_{A,K[1],M})\mu_{H_A(K[1],M),K[1]}(1\otimes\sigma_K^{-1}).$$
For the right side Step 4, naturality of $\tau$, and the defining equation for $v_K$ give
$$F(e_{A,K,M})\mu_{H,K}\tau_{FH,FK}(\chi_\Phi\otimes1).$$
These expressions coincide: substitute Step 4's equality for $e_{A,K[1],M}$ into the first, and use the degree-preserving tensor/shift equality proved in Step 1. Thus the shift square commutes for this actual comparison. Iterating it gives positive shifts; applying its inverse at $K[-1]$ gives negative shifts, and induction gives all integers. The canonical iterated shift identifications therefore preserve this equality.

proof.text:
For a distinguished triangle $K_1\xrightarrow u K_2\xrightarrow v K_3\xrightarrow w K_1[1]$, Step 2 gives the two reversed distinguished triangles. Naturality from Step 3 supplies their squares for $u$ and $v$. To see the last square explicitly, put $a=w[-1]:K_3[-1]\to K_1$. Write $\chi_{\Phi,-1}$ and $\chi_{\Psi,-1}$ for the Step-5 comparisons on $K_3[-1]$. The last arrows are $d_\Phi=\epsilon\chi_{\Phi,-1}\Phi(a)$ and $d_\Psi=\epsilon\chi_{\Psi,-1}\Psi(a)$, where $\epsilon$ is the common reversal sign fixed by the contravariant distinguished-triangle convention. Additivity, naturality for $a$, and the shift square give
$$d_\Psi v_{K_1}=\epsilon\chi_{\Psi,-1}v_{K_3[-1]}\Phi(a)=v_{K_3}[1]\,\epsilon\chi_{\Phi,-1}\Phi(a)=v_{K_3}[1]d_\Phi.$$
Thus all three squares, with their specified signs, commute. This is the required morphism of reversed distinguished triangles in the sense of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Both exact functors here use the same Hom/shift convention; the equation retains its reversal sign rather than discarding it.

proof.text: Fix $M$ and let $\mathcal S_M=\{K:v_K\text{ is invertible}\}$. Exact additive functors take zero to zero, so $v_0$ is invertible. If $f:K\xrightarrow{\sim}L$, naturality says $\Psi(f)v_L=v_K\Phi(f)$; both functorial images of $f$ are invertible, so membership in $\mathcal S_M$ is invariant under isomorphisms. Step 5 conjugates $v_{K[n]}$ to $v_K[-n]$ by invertible shift comparisons. Hence $K\in\mathcal S_M$ if and only if $K[n]\in\mathcal S_M$, for all $n\in\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, localization reduction: zero, isomorphism and shift closure expanded

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] to the morphism of distinguished triangles of Step 6. If two of $v_{K_3},v_{K_2},v_{K_1}$ are invertible, so is the third. Consequently any two vertices of a distinguished triangle in $\mathcal S_M$ force the third into $\mathcal S_M$. In particular the cone of every morphism between its objects lies in it. No finite-Tor, constructibility or boundedness condition has been used.

Let $i:K\to L$ and $r:L\to K$ satisfy $ri=1_K$, and suppose $v_L$ is invertible. Define
$$b_K=\Phi(i)\,v_L^{-1}\Psi(r):\Psi(K)\to\Phi(K).$$
Contravariant naturality gives $\Psi(r)v_K=v_L\Phi(r)$ and $v_K\Phi(i)=\Psi(i)v_L$. Thus
$$b_Kv_K=\Phi(i)\Phi(r)=\Phi(ri)=1,\qquad v_Kb_K=\Psi(i)\Psi(r)=\Psi(ri)=1.$$
So the locus is closed under retracts and hence under direct summands. Additivity and naturality for biproduct inclusions and projections identify $v_{K\oplus L}$ with the diagonal matrix $(v_K,v_L)$, with inverse the corresponding diagonal inverses; hence it is also closed under finite sums. Together with Steps 7 and 8 these are exactly the stated thick-subcategory closure properties. Only existing retract maps are used, so no idempotent-completeness assumption is required.
